source: FDA Food Code 2022
title: Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) Food — Holding Temperatures
text: Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods must be held at 41°F (5°C) or below for cold holding, or 135°F (57°C) or above for hot holding, except during necessary preparation. Cold and hot holding equipment must be capable of maintaining these temperatures. Foods found in the danger zone (above 41°F and below 135°F) for an undetermined time are subject to discard. Inspectors typically verify holding temperatures with a calibrated probe thermometer in walk-in coolers (WIC), reach-in coolers (RIC), and hot-hold units.

title: Cooking Raw Animal Foods — Minimum Internal Temperatures
text: Raw animal foods must be cooked to minimum internal temperatures: poultry, stuffed foods, and reheated casseroles to 165°F (74°C) for <1 second; ground/comminuted meats to 155°F (68°C) for 17 seconds; pork, whole-muscle beef roasts, fish, and eggs for immediate service to 145°F (63°C). title: Cooling of Cooked TCS Foods
